overview: Two Rajasthan icons: Jodhpur's towering Mehrangarh Fort above the blue city, and Jaisalmer's living golden fort with Thar Desert dunes and night camps beyond.
fit: Big adventure for the 10-year-old (forts, camels, dunes). The 4-year-old will love camels and sand; desert nights get cold.
season: November to February is best (8–25°C; cold nights in the desert). March is warm. April–June is extremely hot (45°C+).

gettingThere.detail: Jodhpur to Jaisalmer between the two cities

gettingAround: Hire a cab for the trip; autos inside the cities. The forts involve a lot of walking.

todo.title: Mehrangarh Fort, Jodhpur
todo.why: Huge fort with palaces and an excellent audio guide
todo.book: Lift available up to the palace

todo.title: Jaisalmer Fort
todo.why: A fort people still live in

todo.title: Sam or Khuri dunes camel ride and camp
todo.why: Sunset on the dunes, folk music, night under stars
todo.book: Pick a licensed camp with proper toilets

todo.title: Patwon ki Haveli and Gadisar Lake
todo.why: Carved mansions and a lake with boats

stay.area: Jaisalmer inside or near the fort

food.name: Dal baati churma
food.note: Rajasthani classic, can be made mild

foodTips: Rajasthan is very vegetarian-friendly. Ask for less chilli for the kids.
save: Fly into Jodhpur and out of Jaisalmer (or the reverse) to avoid backtracking
safety: Camel rides: an adult holds the 4-year-old
Desert nights drop to 5°C; warm layers needed
health: Dry air and sun: lip balm, moisturiser, sunscreen
kids: Kids love the camel ride and dune sliding
The forts are big; carry a carrier for the little one

days.plan: Fly to Jodhpur; Jaswant Thada; clock tower market
Mehrangarh Fort and zipline; evening train to Jaisalmer
Kuldhara, then the dunes: camel safari and desert camp
Back to Jaisalmer and fly home
